subject: series

subject: series
synopsis: A series set in the MC2 alternate future timeline following the next generation of Avengers — the children and successors of Earth's Mightiest Heroes — as they form their own team.

synopsis: A series following Lei Ling, a Chinese superhero with wind manipulation powers, first introduced in the New Agents of Atlas, as she defends Shanghai from supernatural and technological threats.

subject: series
synopsis: A Marvel-published Alien series set in the Paradiso colony, delivering atmospheric sci-fi horror in the tradition of the film franchise with a fresh cast of doomed colonists.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Justin Gray and Jimmy Palmiotti's New 52 Jonah Hex series relocating the scarred bounty hunter to 19th-century Gotham City, where he teams with Amadeus Arkham to investigate crimes predating Gotham's legendary figures. Rich period detail and reliably satisfying done-in-one storytelling.

synopsis: Marvel's 1961 monster anthology by Lee, Kirby and Ditko, renamed Amazing Adult Fantasy with #7.

subject: series
synopsis: A science fiction miniseries by William Gibson about time travel and the darkest possible timeline, featuring soldiers traveling back to prevent a fascist future.

subject: series

subject: series
synopsis: Dan Slott's horror-comedy story of a white-collar criminal committed to Arkham Asylum who must survive among Batman's most dangerous villains.
author: Dan Slott

subject: series
synopsis: A Lion Forge Catalyst Prime superhero series featuring Magnus, a man with the ability to enter the minds of comatose patients, who becomes a reluctant hero in a world changed by a cosmic event.

subject: series
synopsis: A digital-first vertical Infinity Comic featuring the Astonishing X-Men in standalone adventures, formatted for mobile reading as part of Marvel's digital-native publishing initiative.

subject: series

author: Derek Landy

subject: series
synopsis: DC's tie-in comic to the Arkham City video game, set in the aftermath of the game's events. Bridges plot threads between the game's conclusion and subsequent Arkham installments for players wanting more story.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Peter Tomasi's prequel to the Arkham Knight game, exploring Jason Todd's transformation into the Arkham Knight and setting up the game's central antagonist for readers who want backstory before playing.
author: Peter Tomasi

subject: series
synopsis: Rafael Grampa's stunning noir reimagining of Batman in a stylized, painterly prestige format.
author: Rafael Grampa

subject: series
synopsis: DC's anthology series running backup stories and short arcs across the Batman family, featuring Grayson, Red Hood, Outsiders, and Signal stories alongside Batman himself. subject: series
synopsis: A prestige horror series casting Batman against a werewolf threat in a gothic, atmospheric Gotham.
author: Rodney Barnes

subject: series
synopsis: James Tynion IV's third Batman/TMNT crossover, in which the worlds merge dangerously, threatening both universes. The third entry maintained the quality of the original while escalating stakes across the shared mythology.

subject: series

subject: series
synopsis: Dynamite's 2018 classic Battlestar Galactica mini by John Jackson Miller: Adama's fleet faces a Cylon threat in the original-series continuity.

subject: series
synopsis: AC Comics' collection series reprinting larger-format stories from their catalog of female superhero and pin-up comics.

subject: series
synopsis: The sequel to Billionaire Island, Mark Russell and Steve Pugh's savage satire of wealth, exploitation, and ecological collapse, with the Cult of Dogs bringing a new layer of absurdist villainy to the ultra-rich dystopia.
author: Mark Russell

subject: series
synopsis: Following Shadowland, T'Challa takes over from Daredevil as protector of Hell's Kitchen, an unusual street-level assignment for the king of Wakanda that explores his humility and adaptability stripped of resources and status.

subject: series
synopsis: A Black Panther tie-in exploring T'Challa's role in the Blood Hunt vampire crisis.

subject: series
synopsis: David López's Panel Syndicate series: Ironhead, the daughter of a famous superhero, deals with her family's legacy in a city full of heroes.

subject: series
synopsis: Chynna Clugston's nostalgic teen comedy series about high-schoolers obsessed with 1980s British pop culture, known for its warm characters and Blondie/New Wave aesthetic.
author: Chynna Clugston

subject: series
synopsis: A supernatural action series from Zenescope set in the Grimm Fairy Tales universe, following a demon hunter in a world of dark magic and biblical monsters.

subject: series
synopsis: A woman whose husband was killed by a unicorn sets out for revenge in a lush fantasy world where unicorns are dangerous apex predators rather than gentle mythical creatures. Elodie Calibrate teams up with a minotaur companion in this subversive action-fantasy that inverts familiar fairy-tale expectations.
author: Zac Thompson

subject: series
synopsis: An annual benefit publication from the Comic Book Legal Defense Fund featuring anthology stories and art.

subject: series
synopsis: Garth Ennis and Facundo Percio's claustrophobic space horror follows the crew of a deep-space freighter after a catastrophic collision with an alien vessel — Alien influence filtered through Ennis's characteristic character work.
author: Garth Ennis

subject: series
synopsis: Justin Jordan and Jonathan Wayshak's tie-in comic expanding the mythology of Call of Duty's zombie mode, following characters navigating the origins of the undead outbreak. Well-crafted for game tie-in material, delivering exactly what fans of the game mode would want.
author: Justin Jordan

subject: series
synopsis: Brian Buccellato and Jennifer Young's horror set in rural Florida traces a community unravelling after a plague begins turning its members into cannibals, weaving Southern Gothic atmosphere with visceral genre thrills.
author: Brian Buccellato

subject: series
synopsis: Mathieu Bablet's earlier work following two artificial beings — one biological, one mechanical — wandering a post-human Earth. A meditative, visually rich SF fable about consciousness, loneliness, and what it means to persist after humanity.
author: Mathieu Bablet

subject: series
synopsis: Wataru Nadatani's gentle slice-of-life manga about a serious office worker who reluctantly adopts a cat and discovers that cat behavior perfectly mirrors video game mechanics. Sweet, funny, and technically accurate about both subjects.
author: Wataru Nadatani

subject: series
synopsis: Jon Rivera, Gerard Way, and Michael Avon Oeming reimagine the Silver Age DC spelunker as a grieving widower drawn back underground by a psychedelic conspiracy. Young Animal at its weirdest and most heartfelt.
author: Gerard Way, Jon Rivera

subject: series
synopsis: A darker companion to Cells at Work!, set in an overworked, unhealthy body where the cellular workforce operates under near-impossible conditions. subject: series
synopsis: Roberto Aguirre-Sacasa and Robert Hack's horror reimagining of Sabrina: in 1960s Greendale, the teen witch must choose between her mortal life and the Church of Night.

subject: series

subject: series
synopsis: A 2006 Civil War tie-in miniseries set against the Superhuman Registration Act backdrop, focusing on mutant politics and the 198 mutants living under government supervision on Xavier's grounds. author: David Hine

subject: series
synopsis: The original Bill Mantlo-created series following Ty Johnson and Tandy Bowen as runaways transformed by synthetic drugs into light and darkness-wielding vigilantes targeting drug dealers in New York's underworld.
author: Bill Mantlo

subject: series
synopsis: Yuu Kamiya and Tsubaki Himana's manga about a world where everything is made of clockwork, following a boy who revives an android girl. Inventive world-building in a mechanical fantasy setting.
author: Yuu Kamiya

subject: series
synopsis: Paul Allor and Nelson Daniel's 2017 IDW Clue: a meta, darkly comic murder mystery at the Boddy mansion narrated by the butler Upton.

subject: series
synopsis: Paul Chadwick's thoughtful series following Ron Lithgow, a political speechwriter whose brain is transplanted into a massive stone body by aliens — and who uses his condition to become an environmental activist and explorer, meditating on humanity and the natural world.
author: Paul Chadwick

subject: series
synopsis: Ed Brubaker and Sean Phillips' interconnected crime noir anthology set in a shared fictional city, each arc following different morally compromised figures navigating the criminal underworld. The definitive modern crime comic — stylish, cynical, and ruthlessly well-plotted.
author: Ed Brubaker

subject: series
synopsis: David Lapham's Crossed miniseries focusing on a rural family's disintegration as the Crossed infection spreads, amplifying his trademark interest in domestic dysfunction and violence into extreme horror territory.
author: David Lapham

subject: series
synopsis: Kenny Porter's DC series reimagining DC's heroes piloting giant mecha suits to fight Darkseid's massive invasion force, combining robot anime aesthetics with DC mythology in an enthusiastic genre crossover.

subject: series
synopsis: A crossover miniseries merging DC Comics' superhero universe with the Rooster Teeth animated web series RWBY, featuring team RWBY encountering DC characters and villains in a genre-blending adventure.

subject: series

subject: series
synopsis: DC's Pride anthology celebrating LGBTQ+ DC characters through stories by queer creators, featuring characters like Midnighter, Extraño, Dreamer, Renee Montoya, and others. A warm celebration of DC's queer history and contemporary representation.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Q Hayashida's (Dorohedoro) space horror/dark comedy about Zaha Sanko, whose skeleton is rumored to grant any wish — making him hunted across the galaxy. author: Q Hayashida

subject: series
synopsis: A crossover between J. Scott Campbell's spy-action franchise and the Evil Dead universe, leaning into the comedy of Abbott and Costello meet James Bond.
author: Nick Bradshaw

subject: series
synopsis: Rich Tommaso's crime anthology set in Red Circle City, weaving multiple criminal storylines with beautiful retro design work and a sophisticated understanding of the crime genre. Tommaso's best work showcases the possibilities of independent crime comics.
author: Rich Tommaso

subject: series
synopsis: Meghan Fitzmartin's Dark Crisis tie-in series exploring the Young Justice team's response to the death of the Justice League, focusing on character dynamics from Peter David's beloved original series. A nostalgic revisit handled with care.

subject: series
synopsis: Paul Cornell and Leonard Kirk's 2010 Dark X-Men: Norman Osborn's leftover villains — Mystique, Dark Beast, Weapon Omega, Mimic — hunt Nate Grey.
author: Paul Cornell

subject: series
synopsis: Reginald Hudlin and various artists' official comic adaptation of Quentin Tarantino's spaghetti Western about a freed slave and a bounty hunter seeking revenge in the antebellum South.

subject: series
synopsis: A miniseries by Robbie Thompson bringing together Sorcerers Supreme from across time — including Merlin, Newton, and an aged Wiccan — to battle an ancient evil threatening all of magical history.
author: Robbie Thompson

subject: series
synopsis: The Eleventh Doctor (Matt Smith) embarks on whimsical, dangerous adventures across time and space in this Titan Comics series. Captures the childlike wonder and hidden grief of Smith's incarnation, with new companions and classic foes.

subject: series
synopsis: IDW's 2015 Donald Duck: European Disney stories newly translated, by Cavazzano, Freccero and others, plus classic reprints.

subject: series
synopsis: A six-issue event series by Jonathan Maberry following Doctor Doom's successful theft of all of Wakanda's vibranium, forcing Black Panther, Shuri, and the X-Men into a desperate global response.
author: Jonathan Maberry

subject: series
synopsis: A military sci-fi miniseries exploring the ethical and human consequences of drone warfare.

subject: series
synopsis: Comics based on the beloved animated series following Scrooge McDuck and his grandnephews on globe-trotting treasure-hunting adventures, capturing the show's blend of excitement and family comedy.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: A horror anthology by cartoonist Jay Stephens presenting illustrated stories of haunted and strange dwellings, with a classic EC Comics sensibility and a retro horror aesthetic.
author: Jay Stephens

subject: series
synopsis: Dynamite's long-running series starring the beloved horror hostess in original comedic horror adventures. Elvira's campy, self-aware wit drives stories that lovingly lampoon horror genre conventions while showcasing the character's enduring pop-culture appeal.

subject: series
synopsis: Mark Millar and Stuart Immonen's space opera about the wife of a tyrant who escapes with her children and a loyal bodyguard. Immonen's kinetic art elevates a plot-driven genre exercise.
author: Mark Millar

subject: series
synopsis: A digital Infinity Comic exploring the 500-year war in the Eternals' history, presenting extended cosmic conflict in vertical mobile format during the Kieron Gillen era of the mythology.

subject: series
synopsis: Matt Sturges and Dave Justus' Fables continuation follows the Shadow Players spy network navigating a world transformed by the events of Fables' conclusion.
author: Matt Sturges

subject: series
synopsis: A Europe Comics series with distinctive visual style and contemporary urban storytelling.

subject: series
synopsis: Modern New Mutants spinoff with character focus and drama.
author: Bryan Edward Hill

subject: series
synopsis: Brian Azzarello and Rags Morales's 2010 six-issue mini uniting Doc Savage, the Spirit and a gun-toting Batman in a pulp-noir world.

subject: series
synopsis: A Junji Ito horror collection featuring stories of grotesque transformation and bodily horror including the unsettling title story, showcasing his early work in the horror genre.
author: Junji Ito

subject: series
synopsis: Frank Miller's landmark noir anthology set in the corrupt, ultra-violent Basin City — seven interconnected stories exploring crime, hardboiled justice, and moral rot told in Miller's revolutionary high-contrast black-and-white art.
author: Frank Miller

subject: series
synopsis: A bizarre arc from Rick Remender's Punisher run in which Frank Castle is killed and literally stitched back together as a Frankenstein monster, joining a community of classic Universal-style movie monsters.
author: Rick Remender

subject: series
synopsis: Wildstorm's horror anthology and miniseries adaptations of the Friday the 13th franchise featuring Jason Voorhees.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: IDW definitive hardcover collection gathering the core IDW G.I. Joe series, including the main ongoing and related titles by Chuck Dixon and Larry Hama.

subject: series
synopsis: Geronimo Stilton's time-travel comics adventure series, visiting significant moments in human history with the franchise's characteristic educational-entertainment blend for young readers.
author: Geronimo Stilton

subject: series
synopsis: A Viking-era spinoff of the Geronimo Stilton franchise featuring mouse characters in Norse settings. Another competent genre extension of the popular children's comics brand.
author: Geronimo Stilton

subject: series
synopsis: Skottie Young's charming all-ages tie-in to both Avengers vs. X-Men and Secret Wars, reimagining Marvel's heroes and the Avengers/X-Men rivalry as kindergarteners in a Battleworld domain; delightfully irreverent and visually exuberant.
author: Skottie Young

subject: series
synopsis: A digital-first Infinity Comic presenting Marvel heroes as adorable child versions in comedic all-ages adventures, an extension of Skottie Young's popular art style in a vertical mobile format.

subject: series
synopsis: Inio Asano's devastating coming-of-age story follows Punpun Onodera from childhood to adulthood, depicted as a simple bird-like figure amid hyper-realistic backgrounds, examining depression, family dysfunction, and existential crisis with unflinching honesty. One of manga's most emotionally harrowing and artistically ambitious works.
author: Inio Asano

subject: series
synopsis: Cocho Harumochi's manga adaptation of the popular mobile RPG, following Gran and his crew of skyfarers in adventure across floating islands. A competent adaptation of the game's world for dedicated fans.
author: Cocho Harumochi

subject: series
synopsis: A crossover event series in the Grimm Fairy Tales universe depicting a war between the various magical realms — Wonderland, Oz, Neverland, and others — as their forces clash in an epic battle. Serves as a culmination of multiple GFT ongoing storylines.

subject: series
synopsis: A Titan Comics original fantasy series.

subject: series
synopsis: Comics adaptation of Art Clokey's beloved clay animation character Gumby, the curious green boy who could enter books and travel through imagination. The 1986–1988 run by Bob Burden (creator of Flaming Carrot) gave Gumby a surreal, adult-humor sensibility that was as odd as it was affectionate toward the original property.
author: Bob Burden

subject: series
synopsis: Robert Venditti's Rebirth-era series following Hal Jordan rebuilding the Green Lantern Corps from scratch in a universe of chaos. Delivers solid Green Lantern space opera with strong ensemble work across the four Earth Lanterns.
author: Robert Venditti

subject: series
synopsis: A Gold Key adaptation of the classic animated series with comedic racing adventures.

subject: series
synopsis: A special ops team descends into Hell on extraction missions, rescuing souls in a brutal action-horror setting reminiscent of military thrillers.
author: Cullen Bunn

subject: series
synopsis: Ben Blacker and Mirka Andolfo's feminist horror satire traps a coven of powerful witches in a perfect 1950s suburb, memories erased and powers suppressed by warlock architects determined to control them.
author: Ben Blacker

subject: series
synopsis: Tamifull's acclaimed yuri romance manga about two college freshmen who enter a casual relationship that gradually becomes something more. Honest, emotionally nuanced, and unusually realistic in depicting the awkward evolution from arrangement to genuine love.
author: Tamifull

subject: series
synopsis: An Age of Ultron aftermath tie-in in which the temporal damage caused by the event tears open the boundary between the main Marvel Universe and the Ultimate Universe, allowing the Ultimate Gah Lak Tus swarm to pour through.
author: Joshua Hale Fialkov

subject: series
synopsis: Action thriller series from MadCave featuring relentless pursuit and survival horror elements in a gritty, violent story of predator and prey.
author: Mark London

subject: series
synopsis: A journalist is hired by a mysterious, wealthy recluse to ghostwrite his memoirs, only to discover her employer is a cat who has lived nine lives across human history.
author: Paul Tobin

subject: series
synopsis: A team superhero series within Lion Forge's Catalyst Prime universe, following a diverse group of individuals who gained powers from a world-altering cosmic event and must work together despite their differences.

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel UK/Panini's annual specials and special editions featuring the Incredible Hulk in longer-format adventures, primarily reprinting key Hulk stories from across the character's history for British readers.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Jason Aaron's Incredible Hulk run in which Bruce Banner and the Hulk are finally and horrifyingly separated into two distinct beings, exploring what each becomes without the other in a psychologically intense thriller.
author: Jason Aaron

subject: series
synopsis: Infinite Frontier: Secret Files (2021), a six-issue series of short stories spotlighting characters in DC's post-Death Metal relaunch.

subject: series
synopsis: Charles Soule's series launching the post-Infinity Inhumans expansion, establishing Black Bolt's kingdom of Attilan integrating a new wave of NuHumans, building the foundation for Marvel's Inhumans push.
author: Charles Soule

subject: series
synopsis: A recent Iron Fist limited series sending Danny Rand on a globe-spanning adventure to save the Seven Capital Cities of Heaven from a monstrous new threat consuming their chi.

subject: series
synopsis: Robert Kirkman's overlooked gem following Eric O'Grady, a thoroughly selfish S.H.I.E.L.D. agent who steals an Ant-Man suit for personal gain, making him one of Marvel's most entertainingly disreputable antiheroes.
author: Robert Kirkman

subject: series
synopsis: French fantasy comic about a half-Irish, half-Japanese warrior woman navigating a world of myth and colonial conflict.
author: Raule

subject: series
synopsis: John Ostrander's seven-issue 2001-2002 series revisiting key eras of Justice League history — the Golden Age JSA, the Silver Age formation, the Detroit era — with new stories revealing untold chapters. A love letter to JLA history by a creator who knows it deeply.
author: John Ostrander
